faqs.a:
(a)
It shall be the responsibility of the property owner of any property served by the
               city water system to provide access for inspection, repair, removal, or replacement
               of water meters, water meter pits, or water meter vaults as a condition of receipt
               of water service. In the event that access as required herein is not provided, the
               city shall notify the property owner of the failure of the property owner to provide
               the required access, and the property owner shall promptly take such steps as may
               be necessary to provide the required access. Failure to provide access following notice
               shall be a violation of
section 102-62
and
section 102-62.1
.
(b)
In the event the city determines that access to a property receiving city water service
               is insufficient for the purposes described in
section 102-62
or
102-62.1
of this Code, or that city access for the purposes described in said sections of
               this article has for any reason been denied by the property owner, then the city shall
               serve notice of such violation upon the property owner in the manner described in
               this subsection (b) of this
section 102-62.2
. Service of notice of a violation may be made by depositing, postage prepaid, a notice
               into the United States Mail addressed to the address of the dwelling or building located
               on the lot or tract of land upon which a water meter pit is located. Such notice shall
               include a certification of mailing signed by the utilities manager or his or her designee,
               and shall be deemed delivered three calendar days after placement in the mail. Notice
               shall also be deemed delivered if conspicuously posted upon the dwelling or building
               located on the lot or tract of land upon which a water meter pit serving such dwelling
               or building is located, or, if personally served upon a natural person 18 years of
               age or older who occupies a dwelling or building or tract of land upon which a water
               meter pit or water meter vault is located. If the owner of record is located at an
               address other than that address where the meter pit or meter vault is located, then
               the owner of record shall be sent notice at the most recent address of the property
               owner as such tract of land or lot is shown in the records of the county.
(c)
The form and content of notice of violation of
section 102-62
and/or violation of
section 102-62.1
of this Code shall be in writing and shall contain the following information and
               advisements:
(1)
The address and/or legal description of the property upon which the water meter pit
               or vault is located;
(2)
A description of the factual circumstance that constitute the denial or insufficiency
               of access;
(3)
A demand that the property owner provide access to the water meter pit or vault sufficient
               to meet the requirements of
section 102-62.1
of this Code not later than ten calendar days from the date of actual or constructive
               receipt of the notice of violation;
(4)
A statement advising the recipient that the property owner's refusal or failure to
               provide access to the water meter pit or water meter vault constitutes a violation
               of this article, and that failure to provide access as required in this article shall
               result in the charge of a $10.00 per day fee until such time as access is provided;
(5)
A statement that continued failure to provide access after actual or constructive
               receipt of a notice of violation may result in the installation of a flow restriction
               device and/or suspension of water service to the property, or relocation of the water
               meter pit to a different location accessible by the city at the cost and expense of
               the property owner;
(6)
An advisement that persons contesting the city's determination of a property owner's
               failure to provide access may file a written request to the utilities manager for
               review of such determination within ten calendar days of actual or constructive receipt
               of the notice of failure to provide access.
(
Ord. No. 4030, § 1, 10-16-2006
)
